searchText: <@240180844130598912> given that there's been a few improvements to trin performance in the last weeks, have you experimented with turning all the state bridges back on again to see how the situation has improved? What improvements are you referring to? https://github.com/ethereum/trin/pull/1700 https://github.com/ethereum/trin/pull/1662 I already tested/deployed these and the Portal Nodes were still getting congested unfortunately (At least those are my assumptions, which can be confirmed* if we deploy Accept Codes) Ok, alternative option? Can you artificially slow down the rate at which the bridges process blocks? How slow do we have to be for things to work? Is it fine if we try this after `Accept Codes` are deployed? Just because `Accept Codes` remove a lot of the guessing from knowing how our bridges perform. I am fine running this experiment after `Accept Codes` are deployed, but it will likely be delayed due to requiring the `pv` rollout. Well `pv` has some initial cost, but after clients implement it it should be easier to ship changes in the future. I remember now, these performance improvements increase the performance of Block Bodies and Receipts on the history network, but not Headers. So these changes wouldn't really make a difference for the State Network. There seems to be a bottleneck around initializing the offer/accept, because Trin is able to send Bodies and Receipts so much faster after those fixes above
